missionPremise: CTX-SITUS-SKIP merged to legacy-design-tools main as 7a739849 (#648): 18,037 rows across Bastrop, Hays and McLennan were frozen on their pre-conformant snapshot because the bake `continue`d past a punctuation-only situs guard refusal before any write; the fix writes an earned absence instead. cloudbuild.publish.yaml pinned one commit behind (3885efad), so the fix reached no image. Source: _dispatches/2026-09-09_ctx-pin_dispatch.md. The deliverable named by the dispatch is not the pin bump itself but proof the change reaches /app/bakes, because the previous pin bump's justification (CTX-MIRROR's 69de8fe6) was measured false by CTX-BUILD's own lane on the same file.

item_whatTheCommitChanges.whatItChangesInMyOwnWords: The conformant bake's per-row loop previously hit a guard, assertSitusNotPunctuationOnly, that correctly refuses a CAD-claimed situsAddress consisting only of punctuation -- but the bake's response to that refusal was to `continue` past the row before writing anything, so an on-roll account with a punctuation-only situs never got baked at all and stayed frozen on whatever pre-conformant snapshot last served it. The fix changes only the bake's RESPONSE to a refusal, not the refusal itself (PUNCTUATION_ONLY_RE and assertSitusNotPunctuationOnly are untouched): the row now writes with baseFacts.situsAddress set to an earned absence (verdict absent-verified, basis quoting the raw offending value verbatim) instead of being skipped, so the account's other facts are no longer discarded along with it. situsCity and situsZip continue to be decided by their own pre-existing, independent logic in both directions. A genuinely blank (never guard-refused) situsAddress claim still bakes a bare null exactly as before -- this earned-absence treatment is deliberately NOT added to the four leaves in BAKE_OWNED_REQUIRED_LEAF_PATHS, which stays exactly what CTX-LEAVES named. The counter previously named skippedBadSitus (incremented but read by nothing) is renamed situsPunctuationOnlyAbsence and now logs per-county to the bake's own stdout, not only the tail JSON summary. A new assertSitusAddressAbsenceEarned fails the bake closed on a malformed absence object or a basis that doesn't name the parcel, mirroring the existing assertRequiredLeafStatesEarned shape. Scale, as reported by the upstream commit message (not independently re-measured by this lane, which has no live-DB requirement): 18,037 rows -- Bastrop 16,104, McLennan 1,165, Hays 768 -- against 1,516,110 total, full-table-scan counted; unblocks Caldwell 48055:1 and McLennan 48309:103671.

section_guardCheck.doesAnythingGuardLdtShaShape: NO. The only shape guard in the full 168-line cloudbuild.publish.yaml is on the DEPLOY DIGEST (`[[ "$$DIGEST" =~ ^${_IMAGE}@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || exit 1`, at the gcloud-artifacts-describe step). _LDT_SHA flows unchecked from the substitutions block into `git fetch --depth 1 origin ${_LDT_SHA}` (line 83). A malformed value -- empty, truncated, or a ref name such as 'main', which the dispatch explicitly forbids pinning to -- would either produce an unguarded git-fetch error or, worse, succeed silently against whatever 'main' resolves to at build time. Not fixed here; not asked for.

LESSON: A relative-import-only recursive tracer (no pnpm install, no full esbuild run needed) reproduces esbuild's actual bundling closure exactly, because bare/package specifiers are always externals or node_modules and esbuild's bundle:true only inlines relative-specifier code. Validate any such tracer by first reproducing a PRIOR lane's already-trusted result before trusting it on something new -- this caught nothing wrong here, but it is the only way to know the method itself isn't the thing that's wrong.

A `git show --stat <sha>` on a commit fetched with `--depth 1` and no parent present locally silently reports the commit as a root (every file as an insertion) instead of erroring -- an all-green wrong answer of exactly the shape DEV_PROCESS warns about. Fetch `--depth 2` (or otherwise ensure the parent is present) before trusting any diff stat on a shallow clone.

An entrypoint list in a build script is itself state that drifts between lanes measuring the same graph on the same day. CTX-BUILD's '4 entrypoints, 26 modules' and this lane's '5 entrypoints, 26 modules' are both correct for the commit each was measured against; the fix is to re-read the entrypoint list from the actual current build script every time, never carry a number forward from a sibling lane's close, even a recent and correct one.
